@graph.headline: Thailand Visa Guide 2026: Choose by Training Length
@graph.description: Thailand's visa exemption dropped to 30 days on 15 September 2026. See which visa fits your training stay, from a weekend to a 5-year DTV.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a visa at all for a short Muay Thai trip?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for most nationalities. If you are eligible for the visa exemption, a trip of up to 30 days needs no visa application at all, just a passport, proof of funds and a return or onward ticket. You only need to think about a visa once you want to stay longer than the exemption, with or without its extension, allows.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I overstay my 30-day exemption?

acceptedAnswer.text: You owe a fine for every day past your permitted stay, and immigration handles the exact consequences case by case. A short overstay is usually resolved on the way out at the airport, but a longer one can mean detention or a future entry ban. If you think you will run past your allowed days, apply for the extension in advance or leave and re-enter cleanly rather than letting the date pass.

mainEntity.name: Can I extend my visa exemption more than once?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The exemption allows one extension of up to 30 days, for a 1,900 THB fee, and it is granted at the discretion of the immigration officer reviewing your file. Once that extension runs out, you need a different visa category to stay longer, or you need to leave the country.

mainEntity.name: Is the 90-day tourist visa the same as the DTV?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, they solve different problems. The tourist visa (TR) tops out at 90 days including its extension, and it is meant for a defined short trip. The DTV runs five years, with 180 days per entry and one 180-day extension, and it is built around a longer commitment such as Muay Thai training as a soft power activity. If your training block is under three months, the tourist visa is simpler. Past that, the DTV is the route that actually fits.

mainEntity.name: Does the 30-day rule change anything for an existing DTV holder?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The 15 September 2026 change affects visa-free entry only. If you already hold a DTV, you still get 180 days per entry and the option of one 180-day extension, handled through Thai Immigration, entirely separate from the exemption rules.

mainEntity.name: What if my nationality is not on the exemption list?

acceptedAnswer.text: Then you need to apply for a visa in advance regardless of how long you plan to stay, exemption timelines do not apply to you at all. The clearest way to check is the official e-Visa portal or your nearest Thai embassy, since exemption eligibility varies by nationality and can change, as the 21 nationalities losing it from 15 September 2026 show.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to show proof of funds even on a short trip?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in principle, regardless of trip length. Immigration can ask to see 10,000 THB per person under the exemption, or 20,000 THB per person if you hold a tourist or non-immigrant visa, with double those amounts for a family and an exemption for children under 12. It is rarely checked at random, but it is a real requirement, not a formality that disappeared, so carrying proof costs you nothing and removes the risk entirely.
